questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Italian culture, history and language has always been interesting to me and i belive that Bologna had a little of everything. Its the oldest functioning univeristy in Europa and has a rich culture in regards of food and political significance

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find information regarding the university, but not that easy in regards to housing and accomodation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A video call with a woman in regards to my arrival in Bologna and some tips about public transport etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I would check many of the facebook groups where people list apartments, but be aware that EXTREMELY many people do want erasmus students living in apartments, so look for housing for the period you are studying early. Many of the people i met during my exchange lived at the Student hotel, so look there also

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I does not matter too much as long as you are living inside of the walls, the city is not that big and you will have maximum like 15 min on foot to almost every class. Bologna also gices student a card for 10 euro where you can take whatever bus in Bologna for free during your stay, so even if you live outside the walls you do not have to walk everywhere.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university didnt help me at all and most people here are not willing to rent places to students or non-longterm workers. I was lucky that i met a guy who had a spare room, and almost had to cancel my stay since i couldnt find anything.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very easy. Their website can be a little hard to figure out, but once you have been there for three minutes it is very clear what they want you to do.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Yes, writing to the emails given to me in the beginning i was able to have every question answered very fast. They also gave me the opportunity to wait signing up for a class untill later.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got registered for every class i signed up for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be very aware that Bologna university is not just in Bologna but also in some of the cities located around bologna, like Rimini, Ravenna etc. This will be written on the describtion of the class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of them were designed to be introduciton courses for exhange students coming to Italy and were quite easy. Some more challenging, but overall a little easier than in Denmark

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite the same with many lectures

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to Italian Culture, Italian Pop Culture, Italian Political Thought, Fashion and Film, Visual Communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Fashion and Film, Visual Communication were very fun and sparked some personal interests, Introduction to Italian Culture, Italian Pop Culture where nice courses to get to learn Italian culture and both old and modern.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Erasmus had many parties and tandem things

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Bologna is a student city so go out and you will meet friends

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Eat food and enjoy the good weather

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Everybody wants to talk

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nonoe

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language, food and people being so outgoing. Also eating out untill late in the afternoon

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Learn some of the language it will help you immerse yourself in the experience. 
Exams have more than one date. So if your course ends in may you will be able to take the exam in August and sometimes semptember without failing it.
Drink wine

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bologna is a small city and it will get very hot in the summer, so be ready to go to the ocean. I can recommend Rimini

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning the language and getting to know students from all around the globe

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: finding housing. You cant wait untill like two months before arriving

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
